architecture_decisions: - AC-01 Spec-first provider authorization: This approved `P2-V0.15.4` specification exists on `ws/app-provider-actions` before substantive provider implementation and passes the protected spec…
work_items: - AC-02 Wave 1 authority reuse: Every provider operation is mediated through the accepted Wave 1 capability/approval registry and exact `ToolAuthorityRequest`/`AuthorityDecision`…
validations: - AC-03 Canonical Project and repository binding: Provider requests require canonical `Project.id` as `project_ref` plus a registered repository/provider target…

AC-05: validate protected requirement — The GitHub adapter provides bounded app-builder branch creation, accepted-lineage commit, and pull-request create/read operations. It exposes no generic Git command/API proxy, force push, merge, deletion, settings mutation, release publication, or unrestricted repository write surface.

AC-06: validate protected requirement — The Vercel adapter provides preview create/read operations bound to canonical Project/repository/source identity. Production promotion, alias/domain mutation, environment/secret mutation, and arbitrary deployment configuration are absent and rejected.

AC-07: validate protected requirement — Successful provider operations return bounded provider/tool/action identity, Project/repository/source identity digests, result identities, normalized status/result codes, and Wave 1 audit records. Given the same typed provider result, safe evidence digests are deterministic.

AC-08: validate protected requirement — Authority denial does not call the provider and produces `DENIED` audit evidence. Provider exceptions or negative typed results produce `FAILED` audit evidence. Neither denial nor provider failure can be represented as provider success.

AC-09: validate protected requirement — Tests prove provider tokens, headers, environment secrets, arbitrary HTTP fields, shell/subprocess fields, hidden reasoning/scratchpads, and raw provider payloads are not accepted by or emitted from the typed provider contracts/evidence.

AC-10: validate protected requirement — GitHub commit and Vercel preview requests require explicit accepted lineage/source revision identity suitable for #60/#61 integration. `applied: true` or arbitrary caller content alone cannot authorize publication, and the provider layer does not redefine protected IMPLEMENT authority.

AC-11: validate protected requirement — Provider fakes or isolated boundaries prove authorized source read, branch/commit/PR, preview create/read success plus negative wrong-Project, wrong-repository, missing/invalid capability, approval mismatch where applicable, generic execution attempt, production-promotion attempt, oversized/malformed input, secret-bearing evidence, and provider-failure behavior.

AC-12: validate protected requirement — The branch carries the committed DSPy compiled plan, passes deterministic Workstream Spec Validation, Parallax P2 CI, and Bounded Autonomy on latest `main`, and has a review-ready PR with explicit #59/#60/#61/#46 interface notes. The worker does not merge or deploy.

protected_acceptance_map.title: Spec-first provider authorization
protected_acceptance_map.protected_requirement: This approved `P2-V0.15.4` specification exists on `ws/app-provider-actions` before substantive provider implementation and passes the protected spec contract gate.

protected_acceptance_map.title: Wave 1 authority reuse
protected_acceptance_map.protected_requirement: Every provider operation is mediated through the accepted Wave 1 capability/approval registry and exact `ToolAuthorityRequest`/`AuthorityDecision` contracts. Repository metadata or provider configuration never bypasses registered capability authority.

protected_acceptance_map.title: Canonical Project and repository binding
protected_acceptance_map.protected_requirement: Provider requests require canonical `Project.id` as `project_ref` plus a registered repository/provider target. Wrong Project, repository, source revision, or target binding fails closed before mutation, and `workspace_ref` is never treated as provider authority.

protected_acceptance_map.title: Narrow GitHub source operations
protected_acceptance_map.protected_requirement: The GitHub adapter provides only bounded repository/source resolution and bounded tree/file reads required for trusted workspace initialization. Paths, entry counts, text sizes, repository identities, and source revisions are validated and bounded.

protected_acceptance_map.title: Narrow GitHub mutation operations
protected_acceptance_map.protected_requirement: The GitHub adapter provides bounded app-builder branch creation, accepted-lineage commit, and pull-request create/read operations. It exposes no generic Git command/API proxy, force push, merge, deletion, settings mutation, release publication, or unrestricted repository write surface.

protected_acceptance_map.title: Preview-only Vercel operations
protected_acceptance_map.protected_requirement: The Vercel adapter provides preview create/read operations bound to canonical Project/repository/source identity. Production promotion, alias/domain mutation, environment/secret mutation, and arbitrary deployment configuration are absent and rejected.

protected_acceptance_map.title: Deterministic safe evidence and audit
protected_acceptance_map.protected_requirement: Successful provider operations return bounded provider/tool/action identity, Project/repository/source identity digests, result identities, normalized status/result codes, and Wave 1 audit records. Given the same typed provider result, safe evidence digests are deterministic.

protected_acceptance_map.title: Denial and provider-failure truthfulness
protected_acceptance_map.protected_requirement: Authority denial does not call the provider and produces `DENIED` audit evidence. Provider exceptions or negative typed results produce `FAILED` audit evidence. Neither denial nor provider failure can be represented as provider success.

protected_acceptance_map.title: Secret and generic-execution exclusion
protected_acceptance_map.protected_requirement: Tests prove provider tokens, headers, environment secrets, arbitrary HTTP fields, shell/subprocess fields, hidden reasoning/scratchpads, and raw provider payloads are not accepted by or emitted from the typed provider contracts/evidence.

protected_acceptance_map.title: Bounded publication lineage seam
protected_acceptance_map.protected_requirement: GitHub commit and Vercel preview requests require explicit accepted lineage/source revision identity suitable for #60/#61 integration. `applied: true` or arbitrary caller content alone cannot authorize publication, and the provider layer does not redefine protected IMPLEMENT authority.

protected_acceptance_map.title: Positive and negative isolated provider tests
protected_acceptance_map.protected_requirement: Provider fakes or isolated boundaries prove authorized source read, branch/commit/PR, preview create/read success plus negative wrong-Project, wrong-repository, missing/invalid capability, approval mismatch where applicable, generic execution attempt, production-promotion attempt, oversized/malformed input, secret-bearing evidence, and provider-failure behavior.

protected_acceptance_map.title: Integration readiness and worker boundary
protected_acceptance_map.protected_requirement: The branch carries the committed DSPy compiled plan, passes deterministic Workstream Spec Validation, Parallax P2 CI, and Bounded Autonomy on latest `main`, and has a review-ready PR with explicit #59/#60/#61/#46 interface notes. The worker does not merge or deploy.
